title: Copilot Dashboard: Copilot configuration recommendations on the Readiness page
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and Microsoft's documentation for the recommendation cards, licensing and dashboard access controls. The Contact admin and Send email steps are accurate, and targeted searches found no documented switch for the recommendation section alone.

The Copilot Dashboard Readiness page now includes tailored Copilot configuration recommendations.

claims.claim: The Copilot Dashboard is hosted in the Viva Insights web app.
claims.quote: If you have access to the Copilot Dashboard, you can find it in the Viva Insights web app. On the left, select Copilot Dashboard.

claims.claim: Steps to enable Copilot and accelerate your AI transformation shows only configuration recommendations relevant to the organisation.
claims.quote:
Steps to enable Copilot and accelerate your AI transformation
This section provides actionable recommendations to enable Copilot Chat, get the most out of Copilot, and activate agents. The page only shows Copilot- and agent-related configuration recommendations that are relevant to your organization.

claims.claim: Users can be added through Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Microsoft Viva > Viva Insights > Set up and management > Microsoft Copilot Dashboard > Manage access settings for Microsoft Copilot Dashboard > Users > Add.
claims.quote:
Go to the Settings tab and select Microsoft Viva, then Viva Insights. On this page, go to the Set up and management tab.
Under Microsoft Copilot Dashboard, select Manage access settings for Microsoft Copilot Dashboard.
At the top, select Users.
At the bottom, select Add.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId "Viva Insights web app" -Name EnableSelectedUsers -IsFeatureEnabled $true -UserIds <user-UPNs> grants feature access to the specified users.
claims.quote:
Policies are used to restrict or grant access to the specified feature for specific users, groups, or the entire tenant.
$true: The feature is enabled by the policy.
The UserIds parameter specifies the user principal names (UPNs) of the users that the policy applies to.

claims.claim: Selecting Groups instead of Users allows Entra ID groups to be added with Add.
claims.quote:
To enable access for new groups:
At the top, select Groups. Search for the Entra ID groups you'd like to add, and select them from the list.
At the bottom, select Add.

claims.claim: The feature-policy cmdlet accepts -GroupIds to target groups.
claims.quote: The GroupIds parameter specifies the email addresses or security group object IDs (GUIDs) of groups that the updated policy applies to. Both Mail-enabled and non-mail-enabled Microsoft Entra groups are supported.

claims.claim: The dashboard access, web app and auto-enablement settings page documents AI Administrator as an applicable role.
claims.quote:
Manage access to the Viva Insights web app for individual users and groups
Applies to: AI Administrator
Enable or disable the Viva Insights web app
Applies to: AI Administrator
Turn off Viva Insights web app auto-enablement with PowerShell
Applies to: AI Administrator

claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Global Administrators can manage all settings on the dashboard settings page.
claims.quote: In addition to the roles described below, all settings can also be managed by Microsoft 365 Global Administrators.

claims.claim: Changes adding or removing users' web-app access take effect in 24 hours.
claims.quote: When you add or remove users to the Viva Insights web app, the change will go into effect in 24 hours.

claims.claim: The Viva Insights web app feature policy controls access to the entire app at tenant, group or user level rather than only the Readiness page.
claims.quote: The AI admin can turn the Viva Insights web app on or off at the tenant, group, or user level using the Viva Insights web app feature access management control in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Turning this control off disables the entire app

claims.claim: The Viva Insights web app is on by default.
claims.quote: The Viva Insights web app is on by default.

claims.claim: Disabling the Viva Insights web app disables the Copilot Dashboard, Copilot Analytics reports and advanced analysis and admin tools.
claims.quote: Turning this control off disables the entire app, which includes the Microsoft Copilot Dashboard, Copilot Analytics reports, and advanced analysis and admin tools.

claims.claim: The Viva Insights web app access policy is created through Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app and feature > Access setting.
claims.quote:
select Viva from the settings menu.
Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access.
Select Create a policy.
Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy.
Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off to enable or disable the feature.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId "Viva Insights web app" -Name DisableFeatureForAll -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone creates a tenant-wide web-app disable policy.
claims.quote:
Example: Turn off the Viva Insights web app for all users in your tenant
ModuleId : VivaInsights
FeatureId : Viva Insights web app
Name : DisableFeatureForAll
IsFeatureEnabled : false
Everyone

claims.claim: The Copilot Dashboard Auto Enablement policy can use Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app and feature > Access setting, applied to Everyone.
claims.quote:
select Viva from the settings menu.
Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access.
Select Create a policy.
Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy.
Select the Access setting option
Select Everyone or Specific people and groups

claims.claim: Auto-enablement is enabled by default.
claims.quote: Default state: Enabled, meaning that eligible users will be auto-enabled for access to the dashboard based on the identification criteria.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no separate admin UI or automation switch to hide the Readiness recommendation cards while retaining dashboard access.

claims.claim: Existing users can be removed through Microsoft 365 admin center > Settings > Microsoft Viva > Viva Insights > Set up and management > Microsoft Copilot Dashboard > Manage access settings for Microsoft Copilot Dashboard > Users > Remove selected users.
claims.quote:
Under Microsoft Copilot Dashboard, select Manage access settings for Microsoft Copilot Dashboard.
To remove access for individual users, at the top, select Users.
Select the users or groups from the list for whom you'd like to remove access.
Select Remove selected users or Remove selected groups.
